Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testOverrideGeoMeanWithMathClass` sets a new GeometricMean implementation by calling `setGeoMeanImpl(new GeometricMean())` on a `SummaryStatistics` instance and then adds data points. The test expects the geometric mean calculated by this overridden implementation to match the direct evaluation using `GeometricMean.evaluate()`. 

Looking at the `SummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl` method, it simply checks if the statistics are empty and then assigns the new implementation. The `getGeometricMean()` method returns the current result from the `geoMeanImpl.getResult()`.

When values are added via `SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)`, it updates several statistical aggregators, including conditionally incrementing the `geoMeanImpl` if it is not the default one (`GeometricMean`). Specifically, `addValue` calls `geoMeanImpl.increment(value)` if `geoMeanImpl` is not an instance of the default `GeometricMean`. In our test, since we replaced `geoMeanImpl` with a new instance of `GeometricMean`, this condition `(geoMeanImpl instanceof GeometricMean)` is true, so `increment` is not called on `geoMeanImpl`. Thus, the new `GeometricMean` override never receives the added values, and its internal state is never updated, causing the computed result to remain incorrect or NaN.

Inspecting `GeometricMean.increment(double)`, we see that it increments an internal `sumOfLogs` statistic, and `getResult()` computes the exponentiation of the average log. Since `increment()` is never called due to the conditional in `SummaryStatistics.addValue()`, `sumOfLogs` remains empty, leading `getResult()` to return NaN.

The root cause of the bug is this conditional in `SummaryStatistics.addValue` that prevents the default `GeometricMean` implementation in `geoMeanImpl` from being incremented. This condition was probably intended to guard against double counting when the implementation is the default one internally managed by `SummaryStatistics`. However, when a user explicitly overrides `geoMeanImpl` with a new `GeometricMean` instance, this logic causes the internal data not to be updated, resulting in incorrect NaN results.

A similar pattern is mentioned in the bug report about replacing the `Variance` implementation leading to NaN in standard deviation, confirming that this conditional pattern causes issues when overriding internal implementations with new instances of default classes.

In summary, overriding internal statistical implementations with new instances of the default classes leads to stale internal state because `addValue()` skips incrementing the new instances due to the `instanceof` checks. This explains the failure in the test where the geometric mean computation yields wrong or NaN results.

---

org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.addValue(double)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.SummaryStatistics.setGeoMeanImpl(org.apache.commons.math.stat.descriptive.StorelessUnivariateStatistic)
